oai_dc:dc.dc:description: “Hermeneutics and Theology” represents Gadamer’s account of the task of theology considered as a human science. Gadamer explicates the relation between discourse and interpretation, situates the uniqueness of religious discourse among other kinds of texts, examines the specific task of Scriptural hermeneutics, and works to adapt his own philosophical-hermeneutical insights to the discipline of theology by way of Aristotelian practical philosophy. In this, he connects hermeneutics and theology as sharing the essential task of providing reflective clarity in service of lived experience and communal practice. Theology is rooted in, and not abstracted from, the concrete situation of the faithful.
